report.board_note: Four of the five Tier A instruments point the same way this morning: GOLD, SILVER, CRUDEOIL and COPPER all imply higher opens (+1.18%, +0.94%, +0.80%, +0.50%), each built on international reference gains of +1.59% to +2.28%. NATURALGAS breaks from that pattern — its reference leg rose only +0.98%, the smallest on the board, and the same -1.07% USD/INR move that merely damped the other four was large enough to flip this one negative, to a -0.10% implied open. The rupee is unambiguously the story today: a single -1.07% USD/INR reading (94.4604 vs 95.48638, TWELVE_DATA, as of 2026-09-02) appears identically as the usdinr_change_pct leg behind every Tier A implied open, doing more work on NATURALGAS than on any other instrument. A third of the board carries no implied open at all: ZINC, ALUMINIUM, LEAD and NICKEL are refused by design because LME publishes before MCX closes, so their only overnight context is a day-over-day LME 3M read, not an open. Within bullion, GOLD trades 0.81% below import parity with a z of -0.04 over 196 sessions — a discount, but an ordinary one — while SILVER is 3.28% rich with a z of 1.20 over 216 sessions; that contrast between an unremarkable gold reading and a moderately elevated silver one is the finding, not either number alone.

report.board_note: The board splits cleanly across all four OI states with no net lean: two instruments show fresh longs (CRUDEOIL, +7,029 contracts to 17,306; ZINC, +97 to 2,673), two show fresh shorts (SILVER, +4,392 contracts to 12,674; LEAD, +177 to 763), two show long liquidation (GOLD, -329 contracts to 10,693; COPPER, -540 to 10,997), and two show short covering (NATURALGAS, -6,905 contracts to 34,072; ALUMINIUM, -84 to 4,365) - a 2-2-2-2 split, with NICKEL's OI state refused outright (the comparison spans 4 sessions and oi_change itself is null). The fragmentation runs within sectors, not just across them: bullion shows both GOLD and SILVER turning bearish over the board's 3-session OI window (liquidation, fresh shorts) even as both carry positive overnight implied opens (+1.18% and +0.94%) - a real gap between recent positioning and the overnight tape confined to precious metals. Energy is split rather than aligned: CRUDEOIL's fresh longs match its own +0.80% overnight gap, but NATURALGAS's short covering sits against a slightly negative -0.10% overnight implied open. Base metals show no complex-wide pattern at all, touching all four states plus one refusal. The clearest outlier is NATURALGAS, carrying both the board's largest absolute OI swing (-6,905 of 34,072 total) and its most extreme COT reading (0.9075 percentile) - the sharpest single positioning signal on the board today. CRUDEOIL is a secondary note: the largest fresh-money OI addition on the board (+7,029 of 17,306) sits against an extreme-low 0.0757 COT percentile.

report.board_note: The dominant structural fact this morning is a total volatility blackout: atr and atr_avg are null for all nine instruments, and dist_to_support_atr / dist_to_resistance_atr are null for all nine as well, while cont_stale_sessions reads 0 across the board — so this is not the staleness path, the ATR is refused outright with no basis beyond the null. That means no instrument's distance to its nearest level can be sized against today's volatility, and no in-play call can be made anywhere on the board; the honest read is that the board has no volatility structure to report, not that it is uniformly coiled or extended. In raw points (not ATR-normalised, and not comparable across instruments of different price scale) the one unambiguous level fact is LEAD, whose dist_to_support reads exactly 0.0 — last_close (196.35) sits on support_level (196.35) itself. Term structure splits contango (GOLD, NATURALGAS, COPPER, ALUMINIUM, NICKEL) against backwardation (CRUDEOIL, ZINC), with SILVER and LEAD each carrying a null term_structure because the board stores no next contract for either this morning (spread_basis: 'no next contract stored'). NICKEL is the board's exception: it is the only instrument with oi_state null and an oi_gap_sessions of 4, versus the uniform 3 sessions carried by every other instrument. On ratios, gold_silver reads 64.41 (per_gram convention — MCX gold quoted per 10g and silver per kg, normalised to rupees/gram before dividing) at the 0.4997 percentile over a 250-session window, with the value drawn from today's actual contracts and the percentile from a back-adjusted continuous series; crude_natgas reads 31.176 (as_quoted convention — rupees per barrel over rupees per mmBtu, a genuinely cross-unit reading) at the 0.7064 percentile over the same 250-session window, actual-contract value against a continuous-series percentile.
